newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists give women a push.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists give women a push.

text.p: France's opposition Socialists said on Wednesday they will run women candidates in nearly one third of all constituencies at the 1998 general election to make good their pledge to boost the role of women in French politics.
Socialist Party spokesman Francois Hollande said Socialist women would run for the National Assembly in 167 -- or 30.9 percent -- of mainland France's 555 constituencies.
The final list of women candidates is to be announced on Saturday. All but three or four of the constituencies were agreed in talks on Tuesday night.
French women have the most dismal parliamentary record in the European Union with just 5.5 percent of seats in the National Assembly, compared to 40.4 percent in Sweden where women fare best.
